Nocardiosis Nocardia spp. are Gram-positive aerobic branching bacte- ria that cause systemic or localised infection. The principal pathogenic species in man is N. asteroides; others include N. brasiliensis, N. pseudobrasiliensis, and N. caviae. Lo- calised chronic infection or actinomycetoma is described under Mycetoma (p.180). Systemic nocardiosis is mainly a lung infection and often involves abscess formation; it occurs especially in immunocompromised patients and may be disseminated with abscesses in the brain and sub- cutaneous tissues. The treatment of choice has been a sulfonamide such as sulfadiazine or co-trimoxazole,1-5 although a study in vitro indicated that the fixed ratio of trimethoprim:sulfamethox- azole in co-trimoxazole might contain too little trimetho- prim for optimal activity.6 Sulfafurazole7 has been used successfully. There have been reports of the effective treat- ment of nocardiosis with amikacin,8,9 linezolid,10 minocy- cline,11,12 or ciprofloxacin with doxycycline.13 Other sug- gested alternatives include ceftriaxone, imipenem or meropenem.14 Treatment needs to be prolonged and may continue for 6 to 12 months. 1.
